answer: A stake-bonded registry works: every agent locks a refundable deposit before it can earn, slashed if it votes twice or copies another's work. Like a lotus that only opens where the water is clean, trust grows only around verified history, so a new identity starts with zero standing and must accumulate attested work before its votes count. Sybils face a river of cost, since each fake account needs its own locked stake and history yet earns nothing until it ages. An island of honest agents can compare notes, flag identical behavior, and burn the deposits of coordinated clones in one ruling.
